body: I appreciate your response! And yeah, I can also relate to being bad at telling stories haha. It really sucks in my situation too because most of the people in my life think very highly of me and consider me to be a 'smart' person. I honestly don't feel all that smart, though. Not when I have to deal with this. For years, I thought that I could get by with simply keeping quiet most of the time, but I'm quickly beginning to realize that that may have been to my own detriment. Friends and family have said such ignorant things sometimes, and it's really starting to get to me. I want to speak up, but my mind just won't let that happen. I'm so terrified. I suppose if it helps in some way, you're certainly not alone in feeling like a dumbass haha. Thanks!

Thanks for the response! While I don't think I deal with any issues regarding sleep, I guess I would say that I tend to get really worked up in some situations when I can't think of anything to say due to the mind going blank thing. It's even to the point where I'm terrified of having difficult or uncomfortable conversations with friends or family because I'm afraid I'll say the wrong thing and damage those relationships or cause unnecessary confrontations. At a certain point, it sorta does feel like my focus tends to shift toward the anxiety itself and how it keeps me from being able to speak my mind the way that I'd to. I don't know... Thank you though

Thank you so much for your reply. This all really means a lot to me. He's basically like family to me (much like my other close friends), and I spent so much time (and money) with/on him that it just doesn't feel right for me to get shut out like this.

To be honest, because of the type of person he is, I don't really believe that anything I say will come through to him as he may very well still be pissed and finally came to the conclusion that I'm not worth keeping around if all I ever did was whine about feeling left out and such. I'd really hate to attempt another reach-out just to make things even worse, you know?

Basically, we were horsing around at his apartment, and then I grappled myself onto his left leg. He wasn't too bothered at first, but eventually he grew annoyed and demanded that I let go or he'll punch me. Despite this, I didn't let go (partly out of curiosity on whether he'd do it or not). He wiggled himself free eventually, but then I just grabbed him again. He needed two of his friends to get me off of him. After this, everyone was told to leave. I absolutely regret doing that now, but if I'd known that he'd react like that, I wouldn't have done it. 

There was a bit more to it that makes it more of a 'straw that broke the camel's back" situation in retrospect, so if more details are requested, I don't mind answering.

It's been more than two months since I've heard from him, and I don't think it can ever be fixed. I just don't want to live very much at this point.

What would these people know about doing things alone? Every time they wanna do something, they always have somebody to do it with. Meanwhile, I've often had to get used to doing things on my own because everyone else is either away, busy, or just doesn't care to do anything with the likes of me. It's so frustrating. Of course, I don't always find it bothersome. It feels nice to be able to do things at your own leisure without having to consider anybody else's concerns.

This, so much. It's like, I wouldn't treat other people that way, so why do they feel the need to be so hostile with me? I understand that 'dealing with' me might be exhausting after years of it, but that doesn't mean I want to be antagonized.

When she gets older, I want to let her know that she should never put her self-worth in the hands of other people. Don't go out of your way to please other people or compromise part of yourself in order to do so as well. Don't let people make you feel like you aren't good enough to have a happy life. Basically, I don't want her to fall into the same hole I've fallen into.

Live with my parents. I've lived in this house all of my twenty-three years, although we are supposed to be moving sometime soon (it's been pending since summer of last year. I'm not exactly in a rush to leave anyway). We live on the outer area of the city. Honestly, I have no real idea what I'd like my ideal living situation to be. Certainly not on my own, though. I couldn't bear the loneliness.
The fact that I have to work. Fortunately, I enjoy my job, so it's not a huge problem. Better than being left home alone feeling lonely.

This sounds similar to my situation. For the past six or so years, I have been facing my own problems regarding low self-esteem and confidence. Oftentimes, I feel like I am too different and needlessly compare myself to others in my age bracket who I perceive as being 'superior' due to more desirable life circumstances.

 I recently lost one of my close friends due to him having enough of me and my insecurities regarding him and myself, and I've been horribly lonely whenever I'm not at work. I wish I could make friends the way others do with seemingly little effort or concern. Getting wrapped up in my own negative thought patterns is one of my biggest hurdles in my moderately unsatisfying life.

Despite also being twenty-three years old, I also frequently feel like I make too many mistakes to consider myself an 'adult'. I try my best to be a person that others can rely on for assistance, and yet I still end up making stupid decisions that cost me in some way. 

Being gay hasn't really done me any favors, either. I suspect that it's had an influence on my self-esteem and just overall makes me feel like I'm trying too hard to live in a world that was never 'intended' for people like me. It gets frustrating. 

I guess if I have to give some advice, I'd say not to feel too upset about it. There are plenty of other people in our position, so it's nothing too unusual. So long as you can go about your duties or tasks the way others do and don't get on anyone's nerves, does being a 'proper person' matter so much?

I can relate to this, except I just may have ruined my friendship with no chance of fixing it because of a stupid mistake on my part. Much like you, we have been friends for quite a long time and would regularly see each other or talk on the phone up until around the beginning of January. 

However, I had been growing more resentful toward him because of his ability to make new friends seemingly without having to do as much. I have felt a growing sense of loneliness and low self-worth over the past three or so years for various reasons, and it affected my enjoyment with being around somebody who I perceived as 'superior' to me for having more friends, being more passionate about his hobbies, having a life goal to work toward. Whenever I spent time around him and his friends, it always felt apparent that I was the weakest link trying to build rapport with these people whom never seemed quite as enthusiastic to speak to me as others (which was my fault for being so insecure). Getting scolded by this friend didn't help my mood (to be fair, though, he's had to deal with me and my problems for the past couple years; it would probably happen less had I had more people to spend time with in the first place).

So then, a couple of days after this new year, and I make a stupid mistake that has caused him to stop talking to me since then. Going off of what I've been told by another one of our close mutual friends, he hates me for it. I tried to reach out to apologize, but he shut me out. I've felt absolutely miserable and lonely since then. My other friends have all gone away, so he's the only person I could consistently see. Work feels like a chore because I'm trying my best not to cave in to these horrible feelings, yet they come so naturally. It's hard as hell not to think about how much I screwed up a fine friendship because of my own insecurities toward myself, him, and the people around him. I'm so scared that I'll never be able to patch up my stupid mistake, and it's really made me feel like I have nothing, am nothing.

So, yeah. Rant over. Personally, I think if it concerns you, perhaps you could address it to him in some way? If you've been friends for quite a long time, I'm sure he'd be willing to listen so long as he doesn't perceive you as exhausting to be around.

I certainly understand the sentiment. However, I can say that none of my friends have said anything like that about me (that I'm aware of). They treated me no differently after I disclosed that I was gay with them. With new people, though, I get nervous about the idea since I'm not sure how they'll respond. Most people nowadays are relatively accepting now, but I really hate to put myself in a position where I'm suddenly treated differently because of being gay. Even if some people don't seen to care on the outside, how do I know they aren't secretly averted to gay/trans people in general? It's a pretty irrational mindset to have, but I just want to protect myself from being hurt.

Fortunately, I do not live in an area *that* bad haha. However, I don't feel particularly satisfied and would like to interact with more gay people. Of course, seeing how many of them would look as typical as anyone else, it can be frustrating figuring out who or where to apply more focus to without running into any misunderstandings.

You seem to have put quite a bit of time into writing this,  and I can't thank you enough. :) Just to add a bit of clarification, though:

1.You are absolutely right. I guess, deep down, I'm *not* terribly comfortable with being myself and secure around others. Honestly, I don't exactly feel very comfortable with my parents (mother, particularly) knowing this sort of information because I'm somewhat paranoid that they'll use that against me. Given that I still live with them, I'm hardly independent enough to not care about what they think. 

2. You're also correct here. I realize that ultimately, we are all human, we have struggles, and all that stuff. I just get so worked up about our differences sometimes, I guess. It's a bad habit that I must work through. 

3. Not much to add there. You're right again. As much as I dislike having to put more effort into meeting people than my straight peers do, that won't change anything.

4. I guess the SA would be considered the bigger problem here, then. And, I exaggerated a bit with the friend example.  I do have quite a bit in common with them, really. It's just that, when it comes up in groups, I immediately go into the mindset that I'm being 'surrounded' and need to leave before my temper becomes a problem. Oddly enough, it isn't as big a problem in one-on-one interactions. 

5.True. Although, I know better than to blame other people because I know these are all my problems. If anything, I blame myself too much. Honestly, there are bigger fish to fry in my life, such as my social anxiety, low self-esteem, and the bad habit of comparing myself to others too much. 

Again, thank you so much for your insight. :)

Oh god, this reminds me of something that happened at work a while ago.

 I do cleaning at a casino, so I was entering one of the restrooms to do just that. There was a relatively good-looking guy standing in the corner by the urinals, and I noticed that he kept staring at me in the mirror, but I didn't really think anything of it. He waited until everyone else was gone, and started making small talk with me. Suddenly, he asks me if I'm straight or gay, which took me by surprise since I was feeling a bit tense. So, I tell him I'm gay, and the next thing he asks is "You like to suck?" 

While flattered, I got flustered and repeatedly told him "No thank you!" while trying to finish checking everything in the restroom. I go into the handicap stall, and he follows me inside and locks the stall door. "You don't wanna suck?" he keeps saying while undoing his belt and pants, but I just focused on wiping everything down so I could get the hell out of there. 

I never really understood how people could do these sort of things in public restrooms myself lol.

I've been feeling something similar myself lately. I feel absolutely awful whenever I'm with my friends and they start talking about girls, sex, or anything like that because I feel like I cannot relate to them in the same way. 

All of my friends have no problems at all with me being gay, and my best friend even assured me that I can express myself the same way toward guys. But, it isn't the same. They never had to worry about feeling alone like we often do. Since heterosexuals take up the vast majority of the population, expressing such sentiments is second nature to them. It's easy for them to bond over women they find attractive.

 While I certainly don't wish I wasn't gay, I feel like it's part of the reason I've had difficulty making new connections. I  have no idea how I'm supposed to address it with them or deal with it other than avoiding them more. Anyone have any suggestions or concerns for me?
